#define kHxFieldEntireStringSize   (-1)

kHxFieldEntireStringSize is used by HxFieldSetSelection and HxFieldInsertText when the caller wants to use the entire string passed as an argument. It is also used by HxFieldDeleteText to indicate that you want to delete to the end of the string.

kHxFieldSelectAll is used by HxFieldSetSelection. It has the effect as if the user had dragged the insertion point from the start of the field to the end. When used, the byteOffset parameter is ignored.

kHxFieldSelectAllReverse is used by HxFieldSetSelection and is similar to kHxFieldSelectAll, but has the same effect as if the user had dragged the insertion point from the end of the field to the beginning. When used, the byteOffset parameter is ignored.

kHxFieldAppendText is used for the byteOffset argument of HxFieldInsertText when the caller wants to add the text to the end of the string.

typedef bool(*) HxFieldFilterCallback(const char *pChar, const char *pText, int32_t newByteOffset, bool firstCharSelected)

Custom character filter When registered via HxFieldSetCharacterFilterCustom, this function will be called before each character insert. If true is returned, the character is allowed, otherwise the character is not inserted into the field.

pChar is a pointer to the character to insert, in UTF-8 pText is a pointer to the field text, and could be NULL newByteOffset is the offset into the string where the char will be inserted firstCharSelected is true if the first character of the field string is currently selected

Enumeration Type Documentation

enum HxFieldAttributes_t

Definitions for field flags.

Enumerator:
kHxFieldDefault  kHxFieldDefault defines a static, single line text field.

used when not setting any attributes

kHxFieldEditable  editable field
kHxFieldMultiLine  multiline field
kHxFieldPassword  only '*' characters drawn.
kHxFieldScrollable  scrollable field
kHxFieldNumeric  numeric field (only '0'-'9', '-', '.' allowed)
kHxFieldNotFocusable  kHxFieldNotFocusable is used internally by compound widgets containing fields (spin buttons and combo boxes). Static fields that do not have a scrollbar are not focusable. This attribute is set automatically for fields that are noneditable and do not have system-supplied scrollbars.

not focusable

kHxFieldCustomScroll  kHxFieldCustomScroll is used by applications that implement scrollbars independently from the associated field. If you set this, the field will send kHxFieldScroll messages when the user interacts with the scrollbar widget, allowing the application to control the top visible line in the field.
kHxFieldNoFrame  kHxFieldNoFrame is set for applications that want a static field that does not have a visible border around it. Editable fields , and static fields that have a scrollbar, should always have a frame to ensure proper drawing of the focus ring.
kHxFieldDontSelectAll  kHxFieldDontSelectAll allows click and drag mouse events to alter the selection when a non-focused field becomes the focused field. Normally, single-line fields always select all, and multi-line fields behave the same as if they'd already had focus.
kHxFieldAutoCorrect  kHxFieldAutoCorrect tells the field code to apply auto-corrections to the field while the user is typing. These are checked when the user hits space or a punctuation key to end the word. To abort the change, the user would hit backspace twice then continue typing. This attribute is ignored for non-editable or password fields.

HxResult HxFieldDelete ( HxField_t *  pField  ) 

Delete a field widget.

HxFieldDelete deletes a field created from an earlier call to HxFieldNew.

It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application, since the widget's parent calls this function just before the parent is deleted. HxFieldDelete only needs to be called when deleting a field at runtime.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field to delete
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxFieldDeleteText ( HxField_t *  pField,
int32_t  byteOffset,
int32_t  byteCount 
)

Delete a range of text.

HxFieldDeleteText deletes the text at the given offset and count. Typically, the offset and count passed by the caller would be those retrieved via HxFieldGetSelection. On exit, the selection will be reset to an insertion point at byteOffset. The byteCount plus byteOffset must be less than the byte count of the entire field otherwise HX_INVALID_ARG will be returned. You can pass kHxFieldEntireStringSize as byteCount to delete from the offset to the end of the field text.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
byteOffset IN: Byte offset into text data to begin deletion
byteCount IN: Number of bytes of text data to delete, or kHxFieldEntireStringSize to delete all text from byteOffert to the end of the field.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL.

HxFont_t **  hFont,
HxColor_t *  pColor,
HxColor_t *  pBackgroundColor,
HxTextFlags_t *  pTextFlags 
)

Get the field font definition.

HxFieldGetFont returns the font, color, and text flags of the field.

hFont, pColor, pBackgroundColor, or pTextFlags can be set to NULL if the caller does not care about the return value for that argument.

The pointer stored in your hFont should NOT be unloaded after it is used, and it is only guaranteed to be valid while the field exists. If you need to keep a copy, use HxFontCopy.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
hFont OUT: Handle to field font, or NULL
pColor OUT: Pointer to field text color, or NULL
pBackgroundColor OUT: Pointer to field background color, or NULL
pTextFlags OUT: Pointer to field text flags, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL.

HxResult HxFieldGetText ( HxField_t *  pField,
const char **  hText 
)

Return a pointer the field text.

HxFieldGetText returns a pointer to the field text.

The handle points to the pointer for the actual text in the field. The text should not be modified directly using the return value, since this would cause the field state to be in error. To change field text, use HxFieldSetText. Any change to the text in the dialog will invalidate this pointer, so you should copy it to your own buffer before making any more HxField API calls or returning to the event loop.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
hText OUT: Handle to the field text
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

pField IN: Pointer to the field
pVisibleLineCount OUT: Number of visible lines
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField or pVisibleLineCount is NULL.

HxResult HxFieldInsertText ( HxField_t *  pField,
int32_t  byteOffset,
int32_t  byteCount,
const char *  pText 
)

Insert text into a field.

HxFieldInsertText inserts the text in the pText argument into the field buffer at the requested offset. After the call, the insertion point is set to the end of the inserted text.

byteOffset can be set to kHxFieldAppendText if the text should be appended.

byteCount is the number of text bytes, not including the null terminator. Alternatively, set byteCount to kHxFieldEntireStringSize to use the entire string length of pText.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
byteOffset IN: Where to insert text as an offset from start
byteCount IN: Number of bytes of text data to insert
pText IN: Pointer to text that is to be inserted
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField or pText are NULL.

HxResult HxFieldIsDirty ( HxField_t *  pField,
bool *  pIsDirty,
bool  flush 
)

Get and set the modified state of a field.

HxFieldIsDirty allows an application to determine the dirty state of a field. A field is dirty after inserting text with HxFieldInsertText or by keyboard input, or after calling HxFieldPaste. A field is not dirty if with a call to HxFieldSetText.

The dirty state is returned in pIsDirty. This argument can be set to NULL if the caller does not care.

The dirty state can be reset to false (not dirty) by setting the flush argument to true.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
pIsDirty OUT: Pointer to state flag, or NULL
flush IN: If set to true, dirty state set to false
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK.

HxResult HxFieldNew ( uint32_t  id,
HxWidget_t *  pParent,
const HxRectangle_t *  pBounds,
HxFont_t *  pFont,
HxFieldAttributes_t  attributes,
HxField_t **  hField 
)

Create a field widget.

HxFieldNew creates a new field widget.

The default system font is used if pFont is NULL. Use HxFieldAdviseHeight to properly define the height of the field bounds so that the frame and focus ring are taken into consideration.

Parameters:
id IN: Unique ID for the widget, defined by app, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
pParent IN: Pointer to "parent" widget containing field
pBounds IN: Pointer to the field bounds
pFont IN: HxFont_t pointer
attributes IN: HxFieldAttributes_t
hField OUT: Handle to the new field; *hField is NULL on failure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails, and sets *hField to NULL.

HxResult HxFieldPaste ( HxField_t *  pField  ) 

Paste text from the clipboard.

HxFieldPaste pastes text from the clipboard into a field.

If the clipboard contains no text, this function returns HX_OK and the contents of the field remains unchanged.

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxFieldSetAttributes ( HxField_t *  pField,
HxFieldAttributes_t  attributes 
)

Set the field attributes.

HxFieldSetAttributes allows you to set the attributes the field.

kHxFieldMultiLine, kHxFieldScrollable and kHxFieldNotFocusable are not valid attributes to reset. They are ignored on input.

HxResult HxFieldSetBufferSize ( HxField_t *  pField,
int32_t  byteCount 
)

Set the size of the internal text buffer.

HxFieldSetBufferSize preallocates a buffer of the given size to hold text data. The default byteCount of kHxFieldDynamicBufferSize (0) causes the buffer to be managed internally, growing as more size is needed.

If the existing text is longer then the buffer space allotted then the text is truncated and null terminated.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
byteCount IN: Fixed number of bytes to reserve for text, or kHxFieldDynamicByteCount
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL.

HxResult HxFieldSetCharacterFilter ( HxField_t *  pField,
HxFieldFilter_t  filter 
)

Set field to use a built-in character filter.

HxFieldSetCharacterFilter controls which built-in character filter is active for a particular field.

Field text will be cleared if the filter is changing to something other than 'none'. The new filter will override any built-in or custom filter that may have been set previously.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
filter IN: New filter to start using
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful, HX_INVALID_ARG if filter is not valid.

HxResult HxFieldSetCharacterFilterCustom ( HxField_t *  pField,
HxFieldFilterCallback  pCallback 
)

Set field to use a custom character filter.

HxFieldSetCharacterFilterCustom registers a user-supplied callback function to be used for filtering input characters.

Field text is not cleared after setting a custom filter; it's up to the caller to clear invalid data from the field if necessary. The new filter will override any built-in or custom filter that may have been set previously.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
pCallback IN: Pointer to filter callback function, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxFieldSetChars ( HxField_t *  pField,
const char *  pText,
int32_t  count 
)

Set the field text using a character count.

HxFieldSetChars copies a given number of chars from the pText argument into the field.

If count is 0, then pText can be NULL, and the field text will be emptied.

Calls to this function send the kHxFieldChanged message. After the call, the insertion point is set to the end of text in the field.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
pText IN: Pointer to text
count IN: Number of bytes of text
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pText is NULL and count is not zero.

HxResult HxFieldSetFirstVisibleLine ( HxField_t *  pField,
int32_t  line 
)

Set the first visible line.

HxFieldSetFirstVisibleLine sets the first visible line in a scrollable field. The line argument is a 0-based line number.

HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if line < 0, or if line > 0 and there are insufficient lines in the field to permit scrolling or the field is not scrollable.

When a field is given focus, the system scrolls the field so that insertion point is visible. Because HxFieldSetSelection and HxFieldSetInsertionPoint sets the placement of the insertion point, calls to either of these functions override calls to HxFieldSetFirstVisibleLine.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
line IN: 0-based line index
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxFieldSetInsertionPoint sets the location of the insertion point using the (x, y) coordinate. If the pByteOffset is not NULL, than the byte offset into the text data for the insertion point location is returned.

int32_t  glyphCount

Set the number of glyphs to use for the display.

Set the number of glyphs to be displayed.

If the existing text is longer then the buffer space alloted then the text is truncated and null terminated.

For example, this function can be used to prevent adding too many digits for calendar year.

HxResult HxFieldSetSelection ( HxField_t *  pField,
int32_t  byteOffset,
int32_t  byteCount 
)

Set the range of the current selection.

HxFieldSetSelection sets the selection range as an offset and count.

byteCount is the number of text bytes, not including the null terminator. Alternatively, set byteCount to kHxFieldEntireStringSize to use the entire string length of pText which will result in selecting part of the string that starts at byteOffset and continues to the end. Setting byteCount to kHxFieldSelectAll or kHxFieldSelectAllReverse will select the entire string, regardless of the byteOffset used.

HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if byteCount < 0. If byteOffset < 0, it is set to 0.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
byteOffset IN: Byte offset into text for start of selection
byteCount IN: Number of bytes of text data in selection
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL.

HxResult HxFieldSetText ( HxField_t *  pField,
const char *  pText 
)

Set the field text.

HxFieldSetText copies the text in the pText argument into the field.

If pText is NULL, then the field text is set to a NULL string.

Calls to this function send the kHxFieldChanged message. After the call, the insertion point is set to the end of pText.

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
pText IN: Pointer to text
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL.

HxResult HxFieldUndo ( HxField_t *  pField  ) 

Swap the current field with the undo snapshot buffer.

HxFieldUndo is a very simple one-level undo.

When there is a field-selection > 0 bytes long (i.e., not insertion point) and that text is deleted or replaced by something else (i.e, via typing), a field snapshot is taken (text, insertion point, scroll-position) immediately prior to the change. HxFieldUndo() swaps that undo-snapshot-buffer with the field. Hence, it is fully symetrical, undo-undo = no-change. kHxFieldUndoSnapshotChanged message is sent, the data being the length of the new buffer (allowing test for 0 to indicate buffer cleared.)

Parameters:
pField IN: Pointer to the field
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
